correctness.rationale: The Chebyshev third-derivative rank proof is valid on (0,1), every quadruple ellipse persists in an open coefficient cone, each five-point determinant is a nonzero polynomial, and finite dense-open intersections give all sizes. In the constrained coefficient spaces, proper hyperplanes can be avoided to realize exactly every subset size at most four. Universal dimension upper bounds and Sauer/thicket inequalities complete the result. An exact rational ten-point witness independently verifies all 210 and 252 determinant subcases, with no numerical extrapolation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader unrestricted class contains hyperbolas and other nonelliptic quadratics, so it may realize traces that a positive-definite diagonal form does not. General unrestricted maximality therefore does not imply this theorem. Here every needed four-point interpolant remains a real axis-aligned ellipse.

Indexed research-record and direct literature comparisons did not reveal a covering theorem; synonym and historical-priority risk remains.
